preamble: Loss of the palatal occlusion of /ɲ/, leaving a nasalized palatal approximant [j̃], i.e. a non-syllabic nasalized [ĩ] that also nasalizes the preceding vowel. This is the usual realization of ⟨nh⟩ in Brazilian and Angolan Portuguese; electropalatographic data show frequent absence of full closure in Brazilian Portuguese. The output is a glide rather than a syllabic vowel.

examples.note: The palatal nasal is realized as a nasal palatal approximant that nasalizes the preceding vowel; [ˈɲĩj̃u] and [ˈnʲĩj̃u] also occur for the initial n.
Contrasts with Sônia [ˈsoniɐ ~ ˈsonʲɐ], where /ni/ is not vocalized.
Like Brazilian Portuguese, Angolan Portuguese realizes /ɲ/ as a nasal palatal approximant.

sources: Shosted, R., Hualde, J. I., & Scarpace, D. (2012). Palatal Complexity Revisited: An Electropalatographic Analysis of /ɲ/ in Brazilian Portuguese with Comparison to Peninsular Spanish. Language and Speech 55(4), 477–502. https://doi.org/10.1177/0023830911434120
Pimenta, H. (2023). Reanalyzing the Phonemic Status of the Portuguese Palatal Nasal Consonant. Diadorim 25(3), e63272. https://revistas.ufrj.br/index.php/diadorim/article/view/63272
